prompt: Write an email to a colleague about missing someone who is far away. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: Thinking of Maya (and a small favor)

Hi Daniel,

I hope your week is going well. I wanted to write to you about something a little outside our usual project updates, because I think you might understand it better than most.

As you know, Maya has been in Singapore since August, and I've been feeling her absence more than I expected. The logistics of a time difference are manageable: we've settled into a rhythm of calls on Sunday mornings for me and Sunday nights for her. What I hadn't prepared for was how many small, ordinary moments would make me notice she isn't here. Last week I saw a bakery selling the odd cardamom buns she loves and stood outside for a full minute, composing a text I couldn't send because it was the middle of her night.

I think that's the hardest part of missing someone far away. It isn't the big occasions, which you can plan around and mark on a calendar. It's the dozens of tiny, unremarkable things you'd normally say out loud without a thought, and which now have to be saved up, or let go. I've started keeping a running note on my phone of things to tell her. Half of them turn out to be trivial by Sunday, but a few are the ones we end up talking about for an hour.

I also keep thinking about how you handled things when your sister moved overseas a few years ago. I remember you mentioning that you two started cooking the same recipe on video call once a month. I've been turning that idea over, and I think I'm going to propose something similar to Maya. Even if the food turns out badly, it feels like a good way to share an ordinary evening instead of just trading updates.

If you have any other ideas that worked for you, I'd really welcome them. I'm not looking for a fix, since the distance is what it is and the reasons for it are good ones. I'd just like to be better at staying close across it.

On the work side, nothing urgent. I'll send the revised timeline before Friday, and I'm happy to go over it whenever suits you. Thank you for always being such a thoughtful person to talk to. It's one of the things I appreciate most about working with you.

Warmly,
[name]
